claims: Bases produce hydroxide ions (OH-) in aqueous solutions.
Bases typically taste bitter.
Bases typically feel slippery.
Bases turn red litmus paper blue.
Bases have a pH greater than 7.
Bases act as proton acceptors.
Arrhenius bases produce hydroxide ions (OH-) in water.
Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is an Arrhenius base.
Brønsted-Lowry bases accept hydrogen ions (H+).
Lewis bases donate electron pairs.
Strong bases dissociate completely.
Weak bases do not dissociate completely.
NaOH is a strong base.
KOH is a strong base.
Ammonia (NH3) is a weak base.
Bases generally have a pH ranging from 7.1 to 14.
Bases have a slippery or soapy texture.
Bases taste bitter.
Bases change litmus to blue.
Bases neutralize acids to form water and salt.
The term base is derived from the concept that bases form the foundation for creating salts when reacting with acids.
Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is commonly known as lye.
Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) is used in construction.
Magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)2) is used in antacids.
